text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, traces split into two kinds: about 54 in 100 contained A25, A26, A27, A28 and A31 but not A36/A37/A42, while about 46 in 100 contained A36, A37 and A42 together with A25, A26, A28 and A31 but not A27; A27 and each of A36/A37/A42 essentially never occurred in the same trace (co-occurrence about 0). [REL011, REL012, REL013]
- In the later window, A27, A36, A37 and A42 each run in essentially every trace (participation rises from about 46–54% to 99.5–100%), and A27 co-occurs with each of them in about 995 in 1000 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, REL011, REL012, REL013]
- The group's placement changed: earlier, A25 led directly to A28 (about 98% of A25's outgoing transitions) and A26 led into A36/A37/A42, which then led on to A31; later, A25 leads into the group (about 98% combined), the group leads to A28, and A26 leads to A27 (about 99%). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Precedence flipped accordingly: A36, A37 and A42 now precede A26, A28 and A31 in about 99 in 100 traces, where earlier they followed A26 and A28; A25 now precedes the group in about 99 in 100 traces. [REL002, REL004, REL006, REL014, REL017, REL019]
- Distances changed consistently: A25 and A28 were adjacent in about 99 in 100 earlier traces and are 4 events apart in about 97 in 100 later ones; the A26→A31 distance was two steps in about 54 in 100 and four steps in about 44 in 100 earlier, and is two steps in about 97 in 100 later. [LAG001, LAG003]
- Mean relative positions moved as expected for this reshuffle: A36, A37 and A42 earlier (about 0.59 to about 0.40); A28 (0.39→0.46), A26 (0.54→0.60), A27 (0.59→0.63, now in all traces) and A31 (0.63→0.66) slightly later; A25 slightly earlier (0.36→0.35). [POS006, POS007, POS008, POS004, POS002, POS003, POS005, POS001]
- The internal order of A36, A37 and A42 remains unfixed in both windows (each pair split roughly 50/50 between the two orders). [REL020, REL021, REL022]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the activities A36, A37 and A42 became a block executed in every case and were placed between A25 and A28, while A27 — previously run instead of this block — is now run in every case after it: the earlier two-variant split (about 54 in 100 traces with A27 and no block, about 46 with the block between A26/A28 and A31) gives way in the later window to a single shape A25 → A36/A37/A42 → A28 → A26 → A27 → A31. This is shown directly and consistently by participation and co-occurrence changes, precedence reversals, successor changes at A25, A26 and the block members, and matching lag and position shifts; with 45 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.7 expected if nothing had changed, the set of differences as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically produces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, REL006, REL013, REL014, REL019, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, LAG003, POS006, POS007, POS008]

Limitations: positions and distances are event indices, not clock time, so the change is established as ordering within traces rather than as a shift in calendar timing; and the evidence cannot rule out that the later window simply contains a different mix of case types (for example only cases that always run the full sequence) rather than a modification of the earlier behaviour. [REL011, REL012, REL013, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]

Other differences: only trace-level noise — a few successor edges appear or disappear at about 0.5–1% of a source's outgoing transitions (e.g. A25→A09/A33/A46 earlier, A25→A02/A08 later), which does not affect the main picture. [DIR001]
